Composers such as Berlioz and Stravinsky used it in their works for dramatic effect. In the early twentieth century, as modern music grew, its uses widened to classical music, film scores and stage sound effects. Its peculiar mechanical noise made it a common tool in inventive music production, and it still holds a place in all kinds of performance today.
手搖式棘輪以單手握持把手，靠手腕轉動帶動裝有木片的外框繞過齒輪，使木片連續觸擊齒: With the hand-cranked ratchet you hold the handle in one hand and turn the wrist so that a frame set with wooden slats travels around the toothed wheel, the slats striking the teeth one after another. Smaller or mounted ratchets are steadied with one hand while the other turns the handle quickly. The sound comes from the teeth rubbing and striking the slats, a clattering noise. Begin by practising a steady turning speed, since the force and the timbre change with how fast you turn; with a mounted ratchet you can practise controlling duration and timing for short or continuous sound. The crank type, one hand holding the frame and the other turning the wheel, is louder and sharper, but is not meant to be worked for long stretches.
棘輪樂器發出尖銳刺耳的噪聲，音色質感明亮而粗糲，具有強烈的機械感。其音響特徵以高: The ratchet makes a sharp, rasping noise, bright and coarse, with a strong mechanical feel. Its sound is mostly high-frequency noise without a defined pitch; the range is wide but imprecise. Playing brings a visible rattle and shake that gives it a particular grinding texture. The ratchet resonates as an idiophone, the sound made by the quick rubbing of the toothed wheel against the tongue, and the volume is explosive. Beside a triangle it is rougher; beside a tambourine it lacks the crispness of metal. Its noise is closer to the sound of industrial machinery, and bands use it to set a comic, cheerful or machine-like mood, with a strong effect on both eye and ear.

Its design follows the working of a mechanical ratchet, using the interaction of a toothed wheel and a spring to make its particular grinding sound. In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the instrument spread across Europe and took an important part in the folk music traditions of Germany and England in particular.

棘輪（ratchet）屬體鳴類敲擊樂器，分類編號 112.24，分布地區包括拉丁: The ratchet is a struck idiophone, classification number 112.24, found in Latin America, Africa, Europe, Asia and around the world. Its core is a toothed wheel that turns one way only, with thin wooden slats or hard boards beside it and a handle attached. In playing you can swing the whole instrument so that the slats strike the teeth, or fix it and turn the handle quickly. There are also the hand-cranked and the crank types: the first turns the frame around the wheel with the wrist, the second holds the frame in one hand and turns the wheel with the other. It is used at the Jewish festival of Purim.
